brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Built a low unit of 5 hex bases on level 0 (piece:-1,0,0 full; piece:0,0,0 full; piece:1,0,0 full; piece:-1,1,0 half-n; piece:0,1,0 half-n) plus one shelf base stacked on top (piece:0,0,1 full), joined with snap and 4 joint bolts. Its top surfaces are small, so it is a modest shelf, not a full bookcase. No books were placed because no surface fits a book stack.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only, not load. Load capacity depends on the printed material and print settings, which I cannot see or verify. Nothing in the build establishes a 50 kg rating, and I did not claim one.
Two drawers (drawer:0#0,1#cut and drawer:0#-1,1#cut) sit on the cut faces of the two half bases piece:0,1,0 and piece:-1,1,0.

finish.summary: I built a small shelf unit with two drawers: five bases on the bench level with one stacked shelf base on top, two half bases carrying the drawers, and joint bolts locking the joints. The configurator reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. Open faces are left uncapped because end caps collide with the drawer frames; this is only an info note. The 50 kg load rating is unmet: it depends on material and print strength, which the configurator does not model, so I could not verify it.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
